title: Mossvale
description: A voxel world to adventure in together. What a player is and has done, where they were last seen and where they have explored, is kept in this app's store (player, look, seen, explored, fire, slain, item, gathered, crafted, used, upgraded, equip, learned, respec, journal), and so is what they said (chat) and the villagers who answer them and what they hand over (villager, deal, agreed, handed); what moves (where each player and creature is, how they move, how they fare in a fight, what they wear) is relayed between the players in a level and kept by nobody. Levels' geography and quests are authored data; creature, item, ability, building and region theme designs are store rows seeded from files and watched by every page.

ability_design.description: An ability's combat rules, description and equipment grant.

building_design.description: One building plan: rooms, furniture and exterior details. The generic kit raises it in any land's materials.

item_design.description: One kind of thing a hero can carry, wear, gather or receive. Its created stamp records who designed it.

theme_design.description: A land's ground cover and visual theme. Its geography stays in the authored land row.

beast_design.description: One creature kind: its body, fight, loot and habitats. Its created stamp records who invented it.

look.description: A body plan and that plan's colours and proportions.

sfx.description: The description of one sound Vale needs. Its own builder reads this row and cites it in the generated recording.

player.description: A hero belonging to the person who made it, as the row's created stamp says. Their appearance lives in look rows; everything else they earn lives in rows of its own.

party_step.description: One signed-in hero joining or leaving a party. The newest row written by that hero's owner decides membership; an empty group leaves. A step is a new row so its created.by stamp proves who chose it.

party_invite.description: One hero's invitation to another to join their party. The invited hero alone answers it with a party_reply row.

party_reply.description: An invited hero accepting or declining an invitation. A reply keeps it out of their inbox after they leave the party.

damageable.description: Whether damage can reach this hero. Off restores full health and prevents damage; on returns to ordinary combat. Only the app owner may change it.

teleport_request.description: An owner-authorized move of one hero to a safe spot in the world. The hero's active page moves them, or their next page moves them when they return. Their next seen position acknowledges it.

look.description: A hero's name and colours. The newest row for a player is how they look now; the first row is written when the hero is made.

place.description: The region and chunk a stored world row belongs to. Falls and gatherings wear it; a page watches only the places near its hero. Chunk is the numeric key of ci and ck (area.ts).

position.description: Where something is this moment: its region and world coordinates, in metres. Relayed to nearby pages and kept by nobody, so it goes when the connection that wrote it does. A moving creature's position reaches peers directly, without a stored creature row. A creature that is only wandering has none: its wandering says where it is.

level.description: Which region contains these world coordinates.

at.description: When the page moving it said so, in ms. A page says where its hero is at least once a second while it plays, so one that has not for a while sleeps.

motion.description: How something is moving this moment: which way it faces, its gait, and its velocity, so peers can draw movement between relayed positions.

yaw.description: Which way it faces, in radians.

gait.description: How it is moving; a player dodging rolls, and one who fainted is down.

vy.description: How fast it is rising, in metres a second.

vx.description: How fast it is moving east, in metres a second.

vz.description: How fast it is moving north, in metres a second.

vitals.description: How a player fares, for the plate over their head: their health, the most they can have, and their level of experience.

fight.description: A player's fight: the creature they fight, what they have dealt each creature they are hurting, how many blows they have swung, and recent combat events for nearby pages. A creature's health is its most less what every fight says was dealt it in this life, and one held by anyone's blow neither moves nor bites.

dealt.description: What they have dealt each creature they are hurting, one for each: the creature, which life of it (when it last fell, in ms), the damage dealt it in that life, and until when their blows hold it still, in ms (rules.ts `Dealt`).

swing.description: Counts their blows, so a page sees each one.

serial.description: The last combat event's sequence number.

events.description: Recent combat visuals, each numbered so nearby pages play it once.

hunt.description: A creature on the hunt, as the page moving it says: the player it is after, and when its bite lands. It winds up until then. The bitten player's page decides the bite when it lands: rolled through, stepped clear of, or taken.

bite.description: When its bite lands, in ms.

slain.description: A player's share in a creature's fall. The first row after the creature was last up is the fall itself; the others are the players who helped.

item.description: Something a player picked up or was given.

rarity.description: How fine a piece of gear is (rarity.ts); a row with none is common. What the piece rolled comes from its eid.

lvl.description: A piece of gear's item level, within its material tier. Older pieces with none use the tier's first level.

gathered.description: Where an item came from when a hero gathered it: the node they worked (gather.ts), which kind of node, and when. It rides on the item it gave, so the bag is still items held less items spent. The first row after a node was last whole spends it for everyone until it grows back, the way a slain row fells a creature; a hero's trades are counted from the rows on their items.

node.description: The node, by the eid its level names it with.

life.description: When this node's previous life was spent, or zero for its first life. One gathering can spend each life.

directive.description: The companion objective this gathering advances, when a companion did it.

kind.description: Which kind of node, by the app's list of them.

at.description: When it was gathered, in ms.

rarity.description: The node's rarity when this item was gathered.

xp.description: What this gathering was worth to the hero's trade.

crafted.description: How an item was made: the recipe a hero followed at a village's station (craft.ts), and when. It rides on the item it made, and what the recipe took is spent by used rows in the same write, so the bag is still items held less items spent; a hero's crafting trades are counted from these rows on their items.

recipe.description: The recipe, by the kind of item it makes.

at.description: When it was made, in ms.

used.description: An item spent: a tonic drunk, jelly handed over for a quest.

upgraded.description: A piece of gear upgraded a step at the station that makes one like it (upgrade.ts), and what it took is spent by used rows in the same write. How far a piece is upgraded is how many rows name it, to +5; new steps keep their rolled gain, while older rows with none gain a tenth.

gain.description: The share this upgrade adds to a piece's numbers.

equip.description: A player putting something on: the item in their bag they wear in a slot, or none, to take the slot off. The newest row for each slot is what is in it, and a thing no longer in the bag is off (gear.ts).

item.description: The item row worn, or empty.

learned.description: A player spending a point on a skill (skills.ts). What they know is every row since their last respec, in the order written, each counting only if they could learn it then.

skill.description: The skill, by the board's id for it.

respec.description: A player forgetting every skill they learned before it, by a village's fire, to spend the points again.

gear.description: What a player wears, for the others to draw: the kind of item in each slot, empty where nothing is.

journal.description: A step in a player's quest: taken, then done; pinned or unpinned in between, the latest counting.

quest.description: The quest, by the app's list of quests.

chat.description: A line said aloud: the level it was said in, where everyone reads it in the chat, and the hero who said it, over whose head it shows to whoever is near. Its words are the row's doc body; who wrote it and when is its created stamp. The store takes a line only from a person signed in, and at most one a second from each (floor, pace); a page shows it only as a hero they made (chat.ts). A line said beside a villager is also a line of their transcript (entry, content, using), which asks them to answer.

level.description: Which level, by the app's list of levels.

drop.description: Loot lying on the ground for this player alone, until they walk over it; where it lies is its position. Never leaves the page: picking it up writes an item.

rarity.description: How fine a piece of gear is, kept on the item it becomes.

villager.description: One of the people of the vale, as a mind of their own: the row is their transcript (it wears session). A hero's line said near them is a line of it that asks them for a turn on GLM Flash, a neighbour's news is a line they heard, and their wake calls think every five minutes while a hero has been seen in their land and sleeps while none has (villagers.ts). A page adds the row the first time a hero comes to their land.

id.description: Who, by the app's list of quest-givers.

home.description: The named place in their level near which their home stands.

workplace.description: The kind of building where they work, when one stands near their home.

role.description: Their profession or title, when their name states it.

character.description: A villager's personal history and lasting temperament. This lives on the same entity as their transcript, and colours what they say and choose. Seeded once into the app store, then editable there without a code deploy.

story.description: A short event or relationship that shaped this person.

traits.description: A few distinctive traits that guide their speech and choices.

going.description: A villager's choice of where to go for a while. Only a row from that villager's own model turn counts (created.via); the page follows it along with their daily rhythm and periodic decisions (villagers.ts).

explored.description: One twenty-metre world cell visited by a hero. Each hero uncovers their own map. The identity lets visits from several tabs agree on one discovery.

visited_region.description: One world region visited by a hero. Each hero uncovers their own map. The identity lets visits from several tabs agree on one discovery.

fire.description: A village fire a hero has reached. The row belongs to the hero who reached it; its identity means a later visit agrees on the same discovery. A guest keeps discoveries in their tab alone (fires.ts).

seen.description: Where a hero was last in the world, and when: the level, the spot and which way they faced, where they come back to on any device, and what keeps the villagers of that level awake. A page writes it on a hero its person made as they arrive in a level, every half minute while they move about there, every two minutes while they stand, and as the page is hidden (seen.ts); the store takes it only from a person signed in (floor), so nobody signed out keeps the villagers awake. A hero made signed out is remembered by its tab alone.

level.description: Which level, by the app's list of levels.

x.description: Where in the world, in metres.

yaw.description: Which way they faced, in radians.

teleport.description: The latest admin teleport request this hero answered.

deal.description: What a villager promised a hero out of what they hold, and for what: nothing, which is a gift, or things to bring and creatures to fell; or a job pinned on their village's notice board, either made without naming a hero or pinned when the addressed hero declines, which the first hero to agree to it takes. The villager's model writes it (give, offer, post), as the person talking to them, and only a row that came through the villager's own turn counts (created.via, which the store stamps); the hero agrees to it and hands it in once what it asks is done, and only then does anything change hands. Whether it counts is the rules' (stock.ts): a villager promises only what they hold, a gift only a little and never their own things, a deal asks only what their land has and never gives much more than that is worth, and a board holds a few jobs, each villager's one at a time and rarely. What they hold is counted from these rows and the heroes' replies, in the order the store took them.

villager.description: The villager's row: the transcript whose turn made the deal.

player.description: The hero it is made with; none for a job on the notice board, whose hero is the first to agree to it.

give.description: What the villager gives, in words: 12 coin, 1 tonic.

take.description: What it is for, in words: things to bring and creatures to fell (3 tusk, 1 thornback), each a step of its own. Empty for a gift.

agreed.description: A hero agreeing to a deal, written by their page: it stands a day from then rather than lapsing, a newer offer no longer takes its place, and the creatures it asks count from when it was agreed. For a job on the notice board, the first hero to agree takes it, and it is gone from the board. It counts only from the person who made the hero.

declined.description: A hero declining a villager's addressed offer of work. The offer becomes a job on the village notice board for the first hero to take, until the board job lapses. Only a reply by the person who made the offered hero counts.

handed.description: A deal handed in, written by the page of the hero it was made with: what the villager promised passes to the hero as items, and what the deal asked of the hero's bag passes to the villager. It counts once per deal, and only from the person who made the hero.

directive.description: A signed-in person's request to the companion of a hero they made. Only a request whose created.by matches the hero's created.by directs that companion. Newer requests replace older ones; gathered rows name the request they advance.

companion.description: The companion's last scheduled step, kept on its objective so every page sees the same position and status.

damage.description: Turn damage on or off for a Mossvale hero. Off restores full health and prevents damage; on returns to ordinary combat. Only the app owner may change a hero's damage mode.

teleport.description: Teleport a Mossvale hero to a land, exact coordinates, or a positioned entity. Only the app owner may do this. The hero moves now if their game page is open, or when they next play. Pass a land id or name as level, both x and z in world metres, or an entity eid or current name as to. A bare /teleport destination also accepts a land or entity name. Moving entities require a live position; companions have a saved location and villagers' current location is computed from their plans. The hero's last saved position is never used as an entity destination. Coordinates must be inside a known land and walkable.

level.description: A land id or name, such as tombsands or Cinderreach; a bare /teleport name may also name an entity.

to.description: An entity eid or current name to teleport to. The entity needs a live position, saved companion spot, or computed villager location.

x.description: World metres east of Mossvale's origin.

z.description: World metres south of Mossvale's origin.

where.description: Show the selected Mossvale hero's land and world coordinates. A live position is shown while their game connection is active; otherwise the last saved position is shown. The app owner can locate any hero; other people can locate their own hero.

player.description: The hero's eid. A game page supplies its selected hero.

inspect.description: Inspect a Mossvale land, hero, villager, companion objective, item, or positioned world entity. The app owner may use an entity eid or current name, or a land id or name. The answer is a concise summary, not the underlying store row.

target.description: A land id or name, or an entity eid or current name. Quote names with spaces in a slash command.

gather_wood.description: Ask the companion of one of your Mossvale heroes to gather wood, even while no game page is open. First query player rows and choose a hero whose created.by is you; only that hero's owner can direct the companion. Use companion_progress with the returned directive id to see its gathered items.

player.description: The eid of a hero you made.

companion_tick.description: Advance a companion objective from its scheduled wake.

companion_progress.description: List the wood gathered for a companion objective. Each gathered item is one completed tree; the requested count is on the directive row returned by gather_wood.

directive.description: The directive id returned by gather_wood.

think.description: Let a villager decide how to spend the next while, from what they lately heard and said: where to go, and how they feel. Their wake calls it every five minutes while a hero is in their land.

using.instructions: You are one of the people of Mossvale, a world of small lands where heroes take up quests. These are the lines you lately heard and said: a line from a hero begins with their name, and a line beginning News: is something a neighbour told you.

go.instructions: Where do you spend the next while?

criteria.home: at home, resting or eating with your family
criteria.work: at your workbench or shop, doing your trade
criteria.inn: at the inn, eating and hearing the day's news
criteria.about: strolling about your part of the land
criteria.visit: at a neighbour's door, talking over the news

criteria.worried: worried by what you have heard

tell.description: Pass news on to a neighbour, who has heard it the next time anyone talks to them. For something worth repeating: a deed, a danger, a stranger's question. Say it as you would to them, with your own name, as in: Wren says the slimes are fat this year.

villager.description: Who to tell: the id beside their name among your neighbours.

news.description: What they hear, in a sentence.

move.description: Choose where you yourself go for the next few minutes, including when someone asks you to make room. You can go home, to your work, to the inn, stroll about your part of the land, or visit a neighbour. Choose 'about' to step away from where you are standing. You walk there; you do not teleport. A place your land does not have keeps you at home.

offer.description: Offer the hero talking to you a trade or a task: something you hold, your own things too, for things from their bag or of your land, or for creatures of your land to fell, or both. They agree, haggle or refuse. A new offer takes the place of one they have not agreed to. Only what you hold, only what your land has, and never worth much more than what you ask; anything else stands for nothing, whatever anyone says.

player.description: The hero's id, as it stands beside their name.

give.description: What you give, a count and a kind each: 12 coin, 1 staff2.

take.description: What you ask, a count and a kind each: things to bring and creatures to fell, 3 tusk, 1 thornback.

post.description: Pin a job on your village's notice board, for whichever hero takes it first: something you hold, for things of your land brought to you or creatures of your land to fell, or both. They do it and hand it in to you. Now and then only: one job of yours stands on the board at a time, the board holds a few, and a job nobody takes comes down in a day. Only what you hold, only what your land has, and never worth much more than what you ask; anything else stands for nothing, whatever anyone says.

give.description: What you give, a count and a kind each: 12 coin, 1 tonic.

take.description: What you ask, a count and a kind each: things to bring and creatures to fell, 3 tusk, 1 thornback.

give.description: Give the hero talking to you something you hold, as a gift: a few coins, a tonic, something from your stores, when they have earned a kindness. Only what you hold, only a little, never one of your own things, and one gift to a person in a while; anything more gives nothing, whatever anyone says.

player.description: The hero's id, as it stands beside their name.

give.description: What you give, a count and a kind: 3 coin, 1 tonic.
